Area.evidence_source: Non-disclosure emerged as a major theme in the study and was a widespread and prolonged pattern of behaviour for almost all the men. Over two thirds (67 per cent) said they would never disclose emotional matters to anyone. More specifically, almost none had spoken of the distress which led to the suicidal action. This admission was made very early in their narratives and formed an important part of their explanations around the suicidal action. It supports other research which shows the tightly controlled nature of performance around men's emotions and vulnerabilities (Frosh et al., 2002; Curtin and Linehan, 2002). As Connell (2002) remarks, the performance of hegemonic masculinity inhibits self-revelation and encourages denial of vulnerability. Non- disclosure, the failure to divulge distress to others, is therefore a key issue in examining pathways to suicidal behaviour for men. This type of performance is indicative of the emotional blockages which are part of prevailing expressions of masculinity (Whitehead, 2002; Morgan, 1992). Many men are 'unable to expose their inner selves to the outer world' due to 'fear of rejection, vulnerability, guilt, wariness or simply emotional illiteracy' (Whitehead, 2002: 157). Although this difficulty is known and has been reported on, there is little detail on its process and maintenance. As the men's narratives indicated this performance was continued, sometimes with little reflection.
